results.summary: This design implements three current-switching DACs for analog VGA display signals, using a 16x16 matrix of unit current sources to convert 8-bit digital inputs to inverted analog current sink outputs. It requires external pull-up resistors and opamp circuits to convert the current outputs to a 0-0.7V range for a VGA display, or can use the TinyVGA PMOD for basic digital RGB222 output. The digital controller generates various test patterns and displays, and the Vbias reference voltage can be set via digital inputs. The design is an experiment in analog VGA signal generation on Tiny Tapeout.

This design is a 60 Hz RMS pump-out controller that turns on a pump every 24 hours and monitors current via a current transformer to detect when a tank is empty, then turns off the pump. It uses an external ADC to measure the current and controls a relay to switch the pump, with LEDs indicating status and a button to start a pump-out manually. The design was tested with RTL simulation at 16x speedup, FPGA emulation, and a development board with a Forge FPGA emulator. It is notable for its thorough testing methodology and system-level approach.

This design implements a USB CDC to UART bridge that allows a computer to communicate with a UART device at 115200 baud. It requires a USB breakout board and a 1.5k ohm resistor to connect the USB D+ and D- lines. The device enumerates as a serial port with vendor_id 1209 and product_id 5454. Silicon test reports confirm it works correctly, including loopback and external UART tests.

This design is a UART template that can be connected to an Arduino for testing. It uses a 7-segment display to show output. The documentation is minimal, providing only basic instructions to hook it up to an Arduino. No further details about the UART functionality or testing are given.

This design implements a customizable padlock that allows the user to set a 3-bit code using switches and then unlock it by entering the code with a push button. It uses a 7-segment display to show 'L' when locked and 'U' when unlocked. No external hardware is required beyond the switches and display on the Tiny Tapeout demo board. The design is a simple educational example of a state machine.

This design is an 8-bit reverse counter with reset, implemented using a series of D flip-flops as a dividing counter. It requires external LEDs connected to all output pins, plus reset and step buttons to operate. The counter counts down on each clock pulse and can be reset to its initial value. It is a simple educational example of a counter circuit.

This design implements a 32-bit Fibonacci linear feedback shift register with taps at registers 32, 30, 26, and 25, producing a maximum-cycle pseudo-random sequence. It includes an initialization/fail-safe feedback to prevent an all-zero state, and allows manual input of a value via switches. The outputs are the eight most significant register bits, which can be observed on LEDs or a logic analyzer. Silicon test reports confirm it generates a random-looking output and works as designed.

This design implements a 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product using full adders. It is a purely combinational circuit with no clock. Testing was done using an IDE. No external hardware is required beyond the Tiny Tapeout demo board. The design is a simple educational example of digital multiplication.

This design implements a 3-bit 8-channel PWM driver that uses a 3-bit counter to generate PWM signals on eight output channels. Each channel has a dedicated 3-bit register to set its PWM level from 0 (always off) to 7 (always on). The PWM level and channel are selected via address and level input pins, and a set pin loads the value. After reset, all outputs are low.

This design provides a P latch and an N latch to test whether they can be properly techmapped and hardened in the Tiny Tapeout flow. The P latch passes its input to output when the enable is high and holds the value when low; the N latch does the opposite. Silicon test reports confirm both latches work as designed. It is a simple test structure for verifying latch synthesis.
